6
A sprinter runs a 100 m race. The sprinter has a constant acceleration from rest of 2.5 m s–2 until
reaching a speed of 10 m s–1. The speed then remains constant until the end of the race.
Which time does it take the sprinter to run the race?
A
8.9 s
B
10 s
C
12 s
D
14 s

hints: Notice the race has two stages: constant acceleration from rest at $2.5 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ to $10 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, then constant speed for the rest of the $100 \text{ m}$.
Use $v = u + at$ for the first stage to get the acceleration time, and $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ to get the distance covered while accelerating.
Subtract the accelerated distance from $100 \text{ m}$ and use time = distance divided by $10 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ for the second stage, then add the two times.
walkthrough: Split the $100 \text{ m}$ into accelerated motion from rest and then uniform motion at $10 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
For stage 1, use $v = u + at$ with $u = 0$, $v = 10 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $a = 2.5 \text{ m s}^{-2}$: $t_1 = 10 / 2.5 = 4.0 \text{ s}$.
Find distance in stage 1 with $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$: $s_1 = 10^2 / (2 \times 2.5) = 100 / 5 = 20 \text{ m}$.
Stage 2 distance is $s_2 = 100 - 20 = 80 \text{ m}$ at constant $v = 10 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, so $t_2 = s_2 / v = 80 / 10 = 8.0 \text{ s}$.
Total time is $t_1 + t_2 = 4.0 + 8.0 = 12 \text{ s}$. This is option C

A.explanation: 8.9 s is too short because it underestimates the distance covered while accelerating from rest at $2.5 \text{ m s}^{-2}$.

B.explanation: 10 s would be the time if the whole $100 \text{ m}$ were run at $10 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, ignoring the 4 s spent accelerating from rest.

C.explanation: 4 s accelerating over $20 \text{ m}$ plus 8 s at constant $10 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ for the remaining $80 \text{ m}$ gives $12 \text{ s}$ total.

D.explanation: 14 s is too long and would imply only about $7 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ average speed, below the actual average of about $8.3 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
